examShortTricks: Trick 1: The title's irony: men dismiss 'trifles' (kitchen things) that actually solve the crime — the women find the evidence the men overlook; this reversal is the core answer.
Trick 2: Evidence of motive: the broken birdcage and the dead canary — Minnie's strangled bird mirrors her strangled spirit; connect symbol to motive.
Trick 3: Gender theme: the men's condescension ('women worry over trifles') is exactly why they fail — quote one condescending line and pair it with the women's discovery.
practiceQuestions: Q. Why is the play titled 'Trifles'? (2 marks) — the 'trivial' domestic details the men ignore contain the motive the women uncover.
Q. What does the dead canary symbolise? (2 marks) — Minnie Foster's silenced joy; her husband killed it as he killed her spirit.
keyPoints: Women find the evidence men dismiss as 'trifles' — gender irony is the core.
The dead canary = motive; discuss the moral choice the women make.
